Ryan from Told Plumbing along with Greg representing REMS Corp. met in the basement of the Knight Building, located at 1 East Center Street, Provo, on the morning or 6 October 2026

The main purpose of the gathering was to winterize the building by turning on the main boiler than services nearly 20,000 square feet of office and restaurant spaces.

The unit was manufactured in 1990 and once a year, a technician initiated a set of sequences that heated water to 180 degrees farenheit and pumped the water to each spaces in the building.

In turn each space or office had a controller that pulled in heated water to create the radiant heat, the old, yet efficient heating method

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The boiler consist of 3 separate systems, water circulation, gas heating and electrical ignition and control

The water circulation was controlled at 35 to 65 psi.

The heated water is pulled to each floor using an in-line pump.

When the water releases its heat the water is returned to the boiler to be re-heated.

It is a closed loop system.

Gas provides the energy to increase the water temperature from room temperature, 80 to 90 degrees up to 170 to 180 degree farenheit.

This heating up takes nearly 2 days and the cooling down takes equally long.

The gas system is similar to home heating, except there is a danger of too much pressure buildup.

There is a pressure sensor and a relief valve that opens to release the water to bring the pressure back down.

The water temperature is set by a limit switch. Turning on the gas heating when the water temperature falls below a certain value.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

After the boiler introduction, Greg took us up to the attic to show us the glycerin based fire suppression,

The clock tower has no insulation and is exposed to elements. The inside temperature would be few degrees higher than outside temperature during winter.

Glycerin freezes at 0 degrees farenheit.

He showed us 3 AHU, air handling units.

North, Middle and South.

He thought one of the 3rd floor units would be replaced.

We thought one of the 2nd floor units was to be replaced next spring.
